sources.title: ATO: Capital gains tax reform
sources.fact: Read 20 October 2026 (published 13 October 2026). States the first stage, the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026, is law and the changes apply from 1 July 2027: cost base indexation replaces the 50% CGT discount for resident individuals, trusts and partnerships on gains accruing on or after that date, a minimum 30% tax applies to individuals on certain net capital gains accruing on or after that date, and pre-CGT assets become subject to CGT on gains accruing on or after that date. An asset held on 1 July 2027 is treated as disposed of immediately before and reacquired on that date, valued at market value or by an apportionment method the Government is still developing; the gain or loss is deferred until a later CGT event. New residential dwellings and assets used to provide affordable housing may keep the current arrangements and the 50% discount by choice.
sources.limitations: ATO guidance that the ATO will update as later stages pass; the apportionment method is not yet enacted. Apply the Act's provisions and application rules, not this page.

sources.title: ATO: Tax reform, reforming negative gearing and capital gains tax
sources.fact: Read 26 September 2026 (page last updated 29 June 2026). States the measures are law and apply from 1 July 2027: negative gearing for residential property investments is limited to new builds, and the 50% CGT discount for individuals, trusts and partnerships is replaced by cost base indexation and a 30% minimum tax rate on capital gains. Properties held at 7:30 pm AEST on 12 May 2026 are exempt from the negative gearing change, and the CGT reforms apply only to gains accruing after 1 July 2027.
sources.limitations: ATO summary. Apply the Act's provisions and application rules, not this page.

sources.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026
sources.fact: Read 26 September 2026 through the Federal Register API (C2026A00049, made 26 June 2026). Schedule 1 inserts cost base indexation for individuals and trusts for CGT events on or after 1 July 2027 (s 110-36(1A)) and Division 119, a minimum rate of tax on capital gains. Schedule 2 inserts s 26-155, which quarantines deductions for residential dwellings used as residential accommodation, with exceptions including a dwelling last acquired before 7.30 pm (ACT legal time) on 12 May 2026 and a new residential dwelling.
sources.limitations: As-made text. Read the application provisions and the ITAA 1997 compilation for the period.
